For dental practices

Social media for dental practices

Patients want to know who they will see, what to expect and whether you are taking on new patients. Here is what to post through the year, what the General Dental Council expects from dental advertising, and how Kanosena can write your posts for you to approve.

Request early access See an example week

Free while we test with our first businesses. Nothing is posted until you approve it.

What’s worth posting

Calm, useful posts that help patients choose you and feel at ease.

  • Whether you are taking new patients

    NHS or private, adults or children. Keep it up to date.

  • Meet the team

    Dentists, hygienists, nurses and reception. Use titles exactly as registered.

  • What to expect

    A first check-up, a hygiene appointment, what happens in an emergency. Plain posts help nervous patients.

  • Oral health tips

    Brushing, sugar, children’s teeth. Useful, easy to share and low risk.

  • Opening hours and emergencies

    Bank holidays, Christmas, and who to call when you are closed.

  • Treatments you offer

    What a treatment involves and who it may suit, without promising results.

Your year at a glance

Moments in the UK calendar worth planning posts around.

January
New year check-ups and practice payment plans, if you offer them.
May and June
National Smile Month, run by the Oral Health Foundation, usually from mid-May to mid-June.
July and August
Children’s appointments before school goes back.
October
Halloween sweets and children’s teeth.
November
Mouth Cancer Action Month, also run by the Oral Health Foundation: a good time to explain what you check for.
December
Christmas opening hours and emergency arrangements.

Rules worth knowing

Social media posts are advertising, so the usual rules apply. These are the ones that come up most in your line of work.

  • Only specialists say “specialist”

    The GDC says only dentists on one of its specialist lists may call themselves specialists. Others must not use titles that imply it, such as orthodontist or periodontist.

    Guidance on advertising (General Dental Council)

  • Don’t promise results

    The GDC says advertising must not mislead or create an unjustified expectation about results. When you promote a treatment on social media, make clear it may not suit every patient.

    Guidance on advertising (General Dental Council)

  • Show GDC numbers

    The GDC expects advertising to include the dental professional’s GDC registration number, including on websites where they are named.

    Guidance on advertising (General Dental Council)

  • No advertising prescription-only medicines

    Anti-wrinkle injections such as Botox are prescription-only medicines and can’t be advertised to the public, including on social media.

    Botox: frequently asked questions (ASA)

General information, checked on 27/11/2026. It isn’t legal advice: check with the body named for your own situation.

How Kanosena helps

You approve. We handle the rest.

  • We read your websiteWe build a short profile of your business, and every fact shows where it came from. You can edit any of it.
  • We write your weekPosts and simple branded graphics in your colours, written only from your profile, with UK dates and seasons in mind.
  • You approve every postApprove, edit, reject or ask for a new version. Only the posts you approve are scheduled.
  • We post and report backApproved posts go out to your Facebook Page, Instagram business account or LinkedIn Page, and we show you how they did.

Questions

Will posts call our dentists specialists?

Only if your website does. Posts are written from your own website, and you check every post before it goes out.

Will you post before-and-after photos?

No. Each post comes with a simple branded graphic in your colours. We don’t create or alter clinical photos.

Which platforms do you post to?

Facebook Pages, Instagram business accounts and LinkedIn Pages for now. Personal profiles aren’t supported.
